newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue chips push Moroccan bourse higher.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips push Moroccan bourse higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock market closed on Wednesday about 1.0 percent higher lifted by blue chip stocks notably and which rose three percent compared with the day before, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 510.36 points from 505.27 points on Tuesday.
"Wafabank and Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur rose three percent boosted by a strong demand," a Casablanca-based broker said.
ONA group, the first biggest holding, rose nine dirhams to trade at 635 dirhams.
Upline Securities said in a recent report that ONA net earnings are expected to reach 852 million dirhams ($92.6 million) in 1996 from 602 million in 1995.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest private conglomerate which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, was up one dirham to 591 dirhams.
The conglomerate has a market capitalisation of more than 5.6 billion dirhams.
In the banking sector, Banque Commerciale du Maroc, one of Morocco's largest banks, remained unchanged at 735 dirhams.
Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique gained two dirhams to close at 180 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie jumped 10 dirhams to 380 dirhams.
Leading stock Wafabank hopped up 19 dirhams to close at 668 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, a blue chip stock, took 13 dirhams to trade at 459 dirhams.
Samir oil refinery, the country's main refinery, gained five dirhams to close at 265 dirhams.
Newly-floated Credor closed unchanged at 593 dirhams.
Traded volume on the official market was 75.5 million dirhams from 76.5 million dirhams on the previous session.
